back: The arithmetic average of a set of numbers.
cards.front: Define the [[kw:mean]] and give its formula.
Calculate the mean of these daily sales: $400, $100, $68, $115, $120, $68, $180.

back: An average where each value is multiplied by its frequency (or weight) before summing.
Used when some values occur more often or are more important.
Grade points (A=4, B=3, etc.) are weighted by credit hours.
A 4‑credit course counts more than a 2‑credit course.
cards.front: Explain how [[kw:grade point average (GPA)]] is a weighted mean.
Compute GPA: A (3 credits), B (4 credits), B (3 credits), C (2 credits).

back: The middle value when data are arranged in order.
Half the values are above, half below.
For an even number of values, median = average of the two middle numbers.

cards.front: Find the median of these salaries: $27,000, $32,000, $40,000, $67,000, $95,000.

back: Even count: average the two middle numbers (30 and 35).
The value that appears most frequently in a data set.
Can have one mode, multiple modes (bimodal), or no mode.
Useful for categorical data or to find the most popular item.
When the data has extreme values (outliers) that distort the mean.
Median gives a better picture of the 'typical' value in skewed distributions.
cards.front: When should you use the median instead of the mean?
What is the blueprint for choosing the best measure of center?
back: [[imp:Conclude:]] choose the measure least affected by outliers or most relevant to the question.
